_comment: Closed whitelist of ORFS/OpenROAD config.mk knobs the LLM agent is allowed to tune for RTL-to-GDS closure.

CLOCK_PERIOD.description: Target clock period. NOT a config.mk key -- ORFS has no such variable; this patches the `clk_period` (or literal create_clock -period) value directly in a working copy of the design's constraint.sdc. Units follow whatever this design's baseline SDC already uses (commonly ns for sky130hd/nangate45, ps for asap7/gf180) -- check get_tunables' current value before changing it, don't assume a unit. Lowering it tightens timing (harder to close setup, may force more area/power to compensate); raising it relaxes timing (easier to close, but the goal is the fastest clock that still closes cleanly). min/max are set per-design at startup, roughly 0.3x-3x this design's original period, so an unreasonable value is rejected rather than silently breaking STA. Set to null via set_tunables to revert to this design's original clock target.

DIE_AREA_SCALE.description: Uniform scale factor applied to this design's DIE_AREA and CORE_AREA rectangles together -- 1.0 is this design's own baseline size (e.g. 0.8 = 20% smaller die and core, same margin proportionally). Only available when this design's baseline already uses ORFS's explicit die/core-area floorplan method -- if this key is absent from get_tunables, the design uses CORE_UTILIZATION instead, which is already this design's equivalent lever (do not expect this key to appear on every design). A last-resort, most-direct area lever: shrink it only after repair flags, margins, and (for utilization-based designs) CORE_UTILIZATION/PLACE_DENSITY are already exhausted -- an aggressively small die will crash placement/routing outright rather than degrade gracefully. Set to null via set_tunables to revert to this design's original die/core area.

CORE_UTILIZATION.description: Target core utilization percent used by the floorplan stage. Your FFT baseline closed at 55.9%.

CORE_MARGIN.description: Margin between core and die boundary, in microns.

MACRO_PLACE_HALO.description: Halo distance (routing blockage) around macros during floorplanning.

PLACE_DENSITY.description: Global placement target density (0-1). Higher packs cells tighter but can hurt routability/timing.

PLACE_DENSITY_LB_ADDON.description: Lower-bound addon RePlAce adds when a placement density retry is needed.

TNS_END_PERCENT.description: Percent of timing endpoints considered during TNS-driven repair passes.

CTS_BUF_DISTANCE.description: Max buffer distance for clock tree synthesis.

REMOVE_ABC_BUFFERS.description: Whether to strip ABC-inserted buffers before placement (1 = strip).

SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN.description: Extra margin (ns) added to the setup timing target during repair passes -- raise this to make the flow repair past 0 slack for more headroom against a stubborn setup violation.

HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN.description: Extra margin (ns) added to the hold timing target during repair passes. Only raise this if hold slack is the actual problem -- it does nothing for setup violations.

ENABLE_PLACE_REPAIR_TIMING.description: Run timing repair during placement using placement-stage parasitics (1 = enable). Fixes setup violations earlier, before CTS/route, instead of leaving all repair to later stages.

OPT_POST_GRT_WNS.description: Run a timing repair pass targeting worst negative slack after global routing (1 = enable, this is the flow default). Turning this off tends to make setup violations worse, not better.

SKIP_LAST_GASP.description: Skip the flow's final aggressive timing-repair pass (1 = skip, 0 = allow it to run). Leave at 0 -- this last-resort pass is often what actually closes a marginal setup violation.

CTS_CLUSTER_SIZE.description: Maximum number of sinks per cluster during clock tree synthesis. Smaller clusters can reduce clock skew/insertion delay at the cost of more buffers.

DETAILED_ROUTE_END_ITERATION.description: Maximum detailed-routing iterations. Raise this if DRC violations are the problem and routing is timing out before it can resolve them; has no effect on setup/hold timing.

CELL_PAD_IN_SITES_GLOBAL_PLACEMENT.description: Extra empty sites padded around each cell during global placement, in site widths. Raising this gives the router more room and can resolve routing-congestion-driven DRC/timing issues, at the cost of density/area.

CELL_PAD_IN_SITES_DETAIL_PLACEMENT.description: Same as CELL_PAD_IN_SITES_GLOBAL_PLACEMENT but applied during detailed placement (finer-grained, after global placement has already run).

MIN_ROUTING_LAYER.description: Lowest metal layer the router is allowed to use (sky130hd default: met1). Raising this frees up low layers for other uses but reduces routing resources.

MAX_ROUTING_LAYER.description: Highest metal layer the router is allowed to use (sky130hd default: met5). Lowering this restricts routing resources and generally makes congestion/DRC worse, not better -- raise it, don't lower it, if DRC violations persist.
